$comment: Every iOS device the app declares an apple-touch-startup-image for.
JSON rather than a module because two very different consumers read it: the
generator (scripts/generate-splash.mjs, plain Node ESM) and the guard
(src/mobile/splash.test.ts, TypeScript under vitest). JSON is the only shape
both read without a build step or a resolveJsonModule decision.
w/h are CSS pixels in PORTRAIT and are what the media query matches on —
iOS does not swap device-width and device-height when the device rotates, so
the portrait and landscape links differ only by (orientation: …). The PNG
dimensions are derived: portrait is w*dpr x h*dpr, landscape is h*dpr x w*dpr.
A device with no matching link falls back to a blank screen, so this list
being short is a visible defect rather than a missing nicety. Adding a device
means adding it here and re-running `pnpm --filter @workspace/edc run
generate-splash`; the guard fails if the links and the files disagree.
